title: Two-fibre product of a framed groupoid
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, with the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix a commutative ring $A$ and $n\geq0$. Suppose each object $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ is assigned a sheaf $H_x$ of $\underline A_T$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every arrow $a:y\to x$ over $u:T'\to T$, suppose given an isomorphism $H(a):u^{-1}H_x\xrightarrow{\sim}H_y$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], satisfying identity and composition equations with the canonical inverse-image associators. Let $\mathcal X^{\mathrm{fr}}(T)$ have objects $(x,\lambda)$ with $\lambda:\underline{A^n}_T\xrightarrow{\sim}H_x$, and arrows $a:(y,\lambda_y)\to(x,\lambda_x)$ satisfying $H(a)\circ u^{-1}\lambda_x=\lambda_y$, using the constant-sheaf comparison. Forgetting the frame gives $q:\mathcal X^{\mathrm{fr}}\to\mathcal X$.
For every $x\in\mathcal X(T)$, the 2-fibre product $h_T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X^{\mathrm{fr}}$ is naturally equivalent over $\mathit{Sch}/T$ to the discrete groupoid with value $\operatorname{Isom}_{\underline A_{T'}}(\underline{A^n}_{T'},H_{x_{T'}})$ at $T'\to T$. In the convention orienting the comparison toward $x_{T'}$, this equivalence sends $(y,\lambda,\phi:y\xrightarrow{\sim}x_{T'})$ to $H(\phi)^{-1}\lambda$. The equivalence is compatible with every base change and its specified $H(a)$ comparisons, including compositions. No hypothesis that objects of $\mathcal X$ or $\mathcal X^{\mathrm{fr}}$ have trivial automorphisms is imposed.

proof.text: Fix $U\to T$ and put $x_U=x\times_TU$ (a chosen cartesian lift). By the fibrewise 2-product definition in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], using the inverse comparison orientation, an object of the fibre is $t=(y,\lambda,\phi:y\xrightarrow{\sim}x_U)$. An arrow $a:t\to t'=(z,\mu,\psi)$ is an arrow $a:y\to z$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ satisfying $\psi a=\phi$ and $H(a)\mu=\lambda$. Here and below identity inverse images are identified by their specified unit isomorphisms. The hypothesis on $H$ gives $H(ba)=H(a)H(b)$ for vertical arrows, so $H(a^{-1})=H(a)^{-1}$. Define $F_U(t)=H(\phi)^{-1}\lambda$, which is an actual module-sheaf isomorphism $\underline{A^n}_U\to H_{x_U}$.

proof.text: For an arrow $a:t\to t'$, $\psi a=\phi$ gives $H(\phi)=H(a)H(\psi)$; hence $F_U(t)=H(\psi)^{-1}H(a)^{-1}\lambda=H(\psi)^{-1}\mu=F_U(t')$. Send $a$ to the unique arrow between these equal objects in the discrete target. Identities and composition are preserved because a discrete category has at most one arrow between two objects. Conversely if $F_U(t)=F_U(t')$, the only possible arrow is $a=\psi^{-1}\phi$. It satisfies $\psi a=\phi$ and $H(a)\mu=H(\phi)H(\psi)^{-1}\mu=\lambda$, so it exists and is unique. Thus no automorphism of a triple survives: when $t=t'$, this arrow is $\phi^{-1}\phi=\mathrm{id}_y$, regardless of $\operatorname{Aut}(y)$.

Define $E_U(

u,\mathrm{id}_{x_U})$ and send the identity of $
u$ to $\mathrm{id}_{x_U}$. The identity equation for $H$ gives $F_UE_U=\mathrm{id}$. For every $t=(y,\lambda,\phi)$, the arrow $\phi:y	o x_U$ is an arrow $t	o E_UF_U(t)$ since $H(\phi)F_U(t)=\lambda$. These arrows form a natural isomorphism: for $a:t	o t'$, both paths are the same arrow because $\psi a=\phi$. Its image under $F_U$ is the identity, and at $E_U(
u)$ its component is the identity. These are the two triangle identities, giving an explicit equivalence of the fibre groupoids.

proof.text:
We check arrows over an arbitrary base map, not just vertical arrows. Let $f:V\to U$, choose cartesian arrows $b:y_V\to y$ and $c:x_V\to x_U$, and let $\phi_V:y_V\xrightarrow{\sim}x_V$ be determined by $c\phi_V=\phi b$, using the lifting property of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Write $k_f:\underline{A^n}_V\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{-1}\underline{A^n}_U$ for the constant comparison. The pulled-back frame is $\lambda_V=H(b)f^{-1}(\lambda)k_f$. The composition equation assumed for $H$ gives $H(b)f^{-1}H(\phi)=H(\phi_V)H(c)$. Consequently
$$H(\phi_V)^{-1}\lambda_V=H(c)f^{-1}(H(\phi)^{-1}\lambda)k_f.$$
The right side is exactly the restriction of $F_U(t)$ in the frame presheaf. For any arrow over $f$ the same computation follows from its comparison square and frame equation. It defines $F$ on the total categories over $\mathit{Sch}/T$.

proof.text:
For $W\xrightarrow{g}V\xrightarrow{f}U$, applying the preceding restriction formula twice gives, after inserting the inverse-image associator,
$$H(c_g)g^{-1}H(c_f)\,g^{-1}f^{-1}(\nu)\,g^{-1}(k_f)k_g.$$
The assumed composition equation for $H$ identifies the first factors with $H(c_fc_g)$; [lem-weil-pbc-constant-pullback-composition-coherence], applied to the abelian group underlying $A^n$, identifies the last factors with $k_{fg}$ through the same associator. Thus this is the direct restriction along $fg$. For identity maps the analogous equality is [lem-weil-pbc-constant-pullback-identity-coherence] and the assumed identity equation for $H$. These are equalities of module maps because both sides are module maps and equality can be checked on their underlying abelian sheaves. This proves composition and identity compatibility, without any flatness or local freeness assumption on $H_y$.

proof.text: The functors $E_U$ also respect pullback: the pullback of $(x_U,\nu,\mathrm{id})$ is $(x_V,H(c)f^{-1}\nu k_f,\mathrm{id})$. The component $\phi$ of the natural isomorphism in Step 3 pulls back to $\phi_V$, since $c\phi_V=\phi b$. Hence $F,E$ and their unit and counit assemble to an equivalence over $\mathit{Sch}/T$. If the chosen lift of $x_U$ is replaced, the lifting property in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] gives the unique comparison over the identity commuting with its arrow to $x$; the formulas already proved apply to that comparison. They therefore give the same equivalence up to its specified natural comparison, and compositions agree by uniqueness. The construction uses the given $H(a)$ for every arrow, establishing all the asserted base-change compatibility.
